items.item_text: 01. All applicants are required to submit responses to the following supplemental questions. Your responses will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise yet specific and informative in your responses to these supplemental questions. "See resume," attachments or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to the questions in the following boxes. Incomplete responses will not be considered. Please indicate below that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes | No

02. I understand that my application will be considered incomplete if any required sections of the application are not completed and/or if any documents that are required are not attached to my online application by the closing date. Options: Yes | No
03. Please specify your highest level of education. Options: High School or equivalent (GED) | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree | Juris Doctor | Doctorate Degree
04. Please indicate the field in which you have earned your degree in:

05. Indicate the full-time equivalent years of formal training, or leadership experience reasonably related to Career Education. Options: Less than one year | One year | Two years | Three years | Four years | Five years or more

06. Indicate where you obtained at least two (2) years of formal training or leadership experience reasonably related to Career Education. 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed. (This section is required)

07. Which of the following best describes your experience overseeing instructional operations, including class scheduling, faculty assignments, enrollment management, FTES goals, and instructional budgets? Options: No experience overseeing instructional operations. | Limited experience assisting with or coordinating instructional operations. | Experience directly managing one or two instructional operations, such as scheduling, faculty assignments, or budgets. | Substantial experience managing several instructional operations, including scheduling, faculty assignments, enrollment management, or budgets. | Extensive experience overseeing multiple instructional operations, including scheduling, faculty assignments, FTES goals, and instructional budgets.

08. If you indicated that you have experience overseeing instructional operations, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

09. Which of the following best describes your experience developing, implementing, or improving Career Education programs and curriculum? Options: No experience in CE program or curriculum development. | Limited experience assisting with CE program or curriculum development. | Experience participating in the development or modification of CE programs or curriculum. | Substantial experience directly developing, implementing, or improving CE programs or curriculum. | Extensive experience leading the development, implementation, and evaluation of multiple CE programs or curricula.

10. If you indicated that you have experience developing, implementing, or improving Career Education programs or curriculum, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

11. Which of the following best describes your experience administering Career Education grants or other educational funding sources, including Strong Workforce Program or Carl D. Perkins funding? Options: No experience in grant administration. | Limited experience assisting with grant administration, budgeting, or reporting. | Experience managing specific grant-funded activities, budgets, or compliance requirements. | Substantial experience managing grants, including budgets, expenditures, reporting, and compliance. | Extensive experience overseeing multiple grants, including budget development, fund allocation, expenditure monitoring, reporting, and compliance.

12. If you indicated that you have experience administering Career Education grants or other educational funding sources, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.
13. Please indicate a demonstrated ability to articulate a meaningful commitment to the college's identity and mission.

14. Describe how you have demonstrated sensitivity and understanding in delivery of services and support to a diverse workforce and student population (diverse in terms of socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic background). This section is required.
Master’s Degree from an accredited college or university in a discipline in which instruction is offered at the college.
Two (2) years of formal training, or leadership experience reasonably related to Career Education.

Directs the instructional operations and activities of the assigned division by developing class schedules, managing faculty workloads, meeting full time equivalent student (FTES) goals, authorizing personnel actions, engaging in employee discipline, and developing instructional budgets.
Analyzes employee performance to develop performance evaluations and address performance issues.
Serves as liaison with K-12 districts and 4-year institutions to promote educational pathways and enrollment.

Participates in the District’s recruitment process to hire full time and part time staff; recommends the hire of departmental managers and full-time faculty to the Assistant Superintendent Vice President of Instruction.
Apportions work amongst subordinate managers, faculty, and classified staff to ensure that the needs of C E instructional programs are being met.
Approves paid time off for all employees under supervision to ensure compliance with collective bargaining agreements, district polices, and that areas under supervision are adequately staffed.
Determines curriculum needs, additions, modifications, and deletions; ensures curriculum changes are compliant with chancellor office guidelines and procedures.
Ensures the accuracy of the District’s course catalog as it pertains to CE instructional programs.
Establishes instructional goals, action plans, and institutional effective plans to obtain short and long-term objectives for CE instructional programs.
Ensures that required assessments such as Student Learning Outcomes (SLOs) and program reviews are completed at the course and programmatic level; ensures the assessment of said outcomes.

Monitors CE grants such as, but not limited to, the Carl D. Perkins and Strong Workforce Program to ensure that grant guidelines and outcomes are being met; directs the identification of outside funding sources for CE and new program offerings.
Administers financial resources to evaluate and approve requests for supplies, equipment, and resources purchased through grant and departmental funds.
Ensures that student support services are provided for all CE instructional programs and areas.

Holds meetings and in-service trainings to facilitate collaborative planning, decision-making, provide Chancellor Office updates as it pertains to CE instructional programs, and keeps faculty and staff informed of District-wide issues and projects.
Directs the preparation of various federal, state, county, and District reports to ensure compliance with regulatory reporting deadlines.
Directs the procurement and distribution of grant funds by preparing grant applications, budgets and reports for local, state and federal grant supported programs.
Establishes partnerships with regional trade associations, economic development agencies, and businesses/industries to identify emerging skills and hiring trends.
Develops partnerships and linkages with business, industry, and the community to procure internship opportunities and other CE objectives.
Serves as the District’s liaison to the Los Angeles, Orange County Regional Consortium; provides leadership for CE advisory committees.
Collaborates with District staff to coordinate and support CE courses and programs.
Performs related duties as assigned
Accrediting Commission for Community and Junior Colleges (ACCJC) Standards
Ensure that CE programs and curriculum are in compliance with CCC Chancellor Office guidelines.
California Community College (CCC) Chancellor Office guidelines for Career Education (CE).
Ensures that class schedules, faculty assignments full time equivalent student (FTES) goals, and instructional budgets comply with state regulations and District policies.
State regulations governing CE instruction in community colleges
Ensure compliance with collective bargaining agreements.
State and Federal regulation regarding mandated reporting
Use ERP software to authorize departmental expenditures.
District policies
Effectively hire, appraise, discipline, and dismiss subordinate employees.
Collective bargaining agreements
Sets the standard and level of service for the CE Department.
Student learning outcome assessments (SLOs)
Effectively follow provisions of collective bargaining agreements and District policies as it pertains to the management of subordinate employees.
Program review assessments
Represent the District in college, regional, and state meetings.
Enterprise Resource Planning Software
Serve on various internal and external committees.
General office software and equipment
Maintain current on any developments impacting CE course curriculum.
Effectively analyze departmental operations to develop short/long term objectives for CE instructional programs, and to determine what support services need to be available for students.
Effectively assess the achievement of short- and long-term goals.
Effectively ensures grant guidelines are being met.
Develop and maintain collegiate relationships with District staff, students, industry partners, and community members.
Apply knowledge of ACCJC Standards to develop accreditation reports and ensure that CE instructional programs comply with such standards.
Use knowledge of state and federal regulations regarding mandated reporting to organize the gathering of information and data in a timely manner.

Apply knowledge of SLOs and Program Reviews to ensure that such assessments are completed in an accurate, timely manner and that such assessments are used to develop/assess short/long term departmental goals and grant outcomes.
Use general office software and equipment to aggregate data, and develop reports, and communicate with District staff and community members.
Communicate effectively, orally and in writing.
